files.lesson.md: --- order: 2 unit: statistics node: AC9M7ST01 n2 title: Mean, median, mode and range summary: "Four numbers that sum up a data set: the mean (add, then share equally), the median (the middle value once sorted), the mode (the most common) and the range (highest minus lowest)." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A team scored 3, 5, 5, 6 and 11 goals. What is a typical game? There are at least three good answers, and they are all useful." connection: power-bill # data/connections/maths.yml (pilot: Make on paper and Also used in; documentation only) app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8180 url: http://127.0.0.1:8180/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: data.yml#explain, caption: "3, 5, 5, 6, 11: mean 6 (▲), median 5 (dashed), mode 5, range 11 − 3 = 8 (arrow)." } explainClip: query: { code: "@data.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Four numbers that sum up the data" say: "Four numbers sum up a data set." clip: - caption: { text: "Mean: add them (30) and share between 5 games: 6.", say: "The mean: add them all, then share equally. Thirty shared by five is six." } - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "Median: the middle value once sorted: 3, 5, [5], 6, 11.", say: "The median is the middle value, once they are in order: five." } - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "Mode: the most common: 5. Range: 11 − 3 = 8.", say: "The mode is the most common, five. The range is eleven take three: eight." } - wait: 1400 --- A data set can have many values. To describe it in a few numbers, statisticians use **measures of centre** (what is typical) and of **spread** (how varied). ## Predict: a typical game ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to the mean of 3, 5, 5, 6, 11 before the board shows it brings out whether they share equally or pick a middle or common value." check: type: predict q: "A team scored $3, 5, 5, 6$ and $11$ goals in five games. What is the mean?" options: - "$6$" - "$5$" - "$8$" - "$5.5$" actual: "6. The total is 3 + 5 + 5 + 6 + 11 = 30, shared equally between 5 games is 6. (5 is the median and the mode; 8 is the range.)" ``` What would you do with the five scores to get one number? ## Run: move the mean ```step stage: run insight: "Adding a value and watching the mean, median and mode move shows how each responds: the mean feels every value, the median only the order." try: { playground: board, starter: "data.yml#run", height: 560 } check: { type: board, text: "Add one more game so that the mean becomes exactly 7. Was your prediction right about the first mean?", when: "n = 6 and m = 7" } ``` Watch the triangle (mean) and the dashed line (median) as you add values. Which moves more when you add a big score? Here are the four measures: - the **mean**: add all the values, then divide by how many there are; - the **median**: sort the values; it is the middle one (or halfway between the two middle ones); - the **mode**: the value that appears most often; - the **range**: highest minus lowest, a simple measure of spread. ## Investigate: the four measures ```step stage: investigate insight: "Mean = total ÷ count; median = middle of the sorted list (average the two middle values for an even count); mode = most common; range = highest − lowest. Leo's mistake takes the middle of the unsorted list." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Find the median of $8, 3, 9, 4, 6, 7$." answer: "6.5" feedback: - ["4", "Sort first: 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9."] - ["6", "With 6 values there are two middle ones: 6 and 7. Halfway is 6.5."] - ["7", "With 6 values there are two middle ones: 6 and 7. Halfway is 6.5."] explain: "Sorted: 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9. The two middle values are 6 and 7, so the median is 6.5." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#leo" text: "Leo finds a median. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: median-unsorted explain: "Line 3: sort first. 2, 4, 5, 7, 9: the 3rd value is 5, so the median is 5." - check: type: answer q: "Find the mean of $4, 8, 9, 3$." answer: "6" feedback: - ["24", "That is the total. Share it between 4 values."] - ["8.5", "That is not the mean: add all four, then share: 24 ÷ 4."] explain: "4 + 8 + 9 + 3 = 24, and 24 ÷ 4 = 6." ``` ### Mean, median, mode, range Here is each measure for the goals data. ```worked 3, 5, 5, 6, 11 :: The data, sorted (the median and range need it sorted). \text{mean} = \tfrac{3 + 5 + 5 + 6 + 11}{5} = \tfrac{30}{5} = 6 :: Add, then divide by how many. \text{median} = 5 :: The middle (3rd of 5) value of the sorted list. \text{mode} = 5 :: The most common value (it appears twice). \text{range} = 11 - 3 = 8 :: Highest minus lowest. 8, 3, 9, 4, 6, 7 \to 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 :: An even count: sort, then the median is halfway between the two middle values, $\tfrac{6 + 7}{2} = 6.5$. ``` Now find the median of $8, 3, 9, 4, 6, 7$. ### Find the mistake Read Leo's working. What must you do before finding the middle? ### The mean ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: two modes, no mode, a range with negatives, then the edge case of a value that leaves the median unchanged." try: { playground: board, starter: "data.yml#median", height: 560 } tasks: - check: type: question q: "What is the mode of $3, 4, 4, 6, 6, 9$?" options: ["4 and 6 (two modes)", "5", "There is no mode"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "5 is not in the data. The mode is a value that appears most often.", "4 and 6 both appear twice, more than any other."] explain: "4 and 6 each appear twice: the data has two modes." - check: type: question q: "What is the mode of $2, 5, 7, 9$?" options: ["There is no mode: every value appears once", "2", "9"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "2 appears only once, like the others.", "9 appears only once, like the others."] explain: "No value appears more than once, so there is no mode." - check: type: answer q: "Temperatures over four mornings were $-3, 2, 5, -1$ °C. Find the range." answer: "8" feedback: - ["2", "Highest minus lowest: 5 − (−3)."] - ["6", "The lowest is −3, not −1."] explain: "5 − (−3) = 8 degrees." - starter: "data.yml#median" hint: ["The median of 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 is 6.", "Which value could you add so 6 is still in the middle?"] check: { type: board, text: "Edge case: add one value so the median is still 6.", when: "n = 6 and d = 6", explain: "Adding 6 itself: 2, 4, 6, 6, 8, 10 has two middle values 6 and 6, so the median stays 6." } ``` ### Two modes Each task changes one thing. ### No mode ### Range with negatives ### Keep the median ## Practise: the four measures ```step stage: practise insight: "Each measure from a fresh data set, mixed; sorting before the median is planted again; the review keeps discrete and continuous fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Find the mean of $12, 15, 9, 14$." answer: "12.5" feedback: - ["50", "That is the total. Divide by 4."] explain: "50 ÷ 4 = 12.5." - check: type: answer q: "Find the median of $21, 17, 30, 25, 19$." answer: "21" feedback: - ["30", "Sort first: 17, 19, 21, 25, 30."] explain: "Sorted: 17, 19, 21, 25, 30. The middle value is 21." smaller: check: { type: number, q: "Put 21, 17, 30, 25, 19 in order, smallest first. What number comes fourth?", answer: 25, tolerance: 0, feedback: [[21, "That's the third in order. Count one more along."], [30, "That's the last one in order. Count along from 17."]], explain: "In order: 17, 19, 21, 25, 30. The fourth is 25. Now which one is in the middle?" } - check: type: answer q: "Find the range of $4.5, 7.2, 3.9, 6.1$." answer: "3.3" feedback: - ["2.7", "Lowest is 3.9, not 4.5."] explain: "7.2 − 3.9 = 3.3." - check: type: question q: "Review: the number of pets in each house. Discrete or continuous?" options: ["Discrete", "Continuous"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Pets are counted."] explain: "Counted: discrete." ``` ### Mean ### Median ### Range ### Review: kinds of data ## Make: build a data set ```step stage: make insight: "Building five values with a given mean and median reverses the lesson: the median fixes the middle value, the mean fixes the total." try: { playground: board, starter: "data.yml#make", height: 560 } hint: ["The median of 5 values is the 3rd once sorted: make it 5.", "A mean of 6 with 5 values needs a total of 30."] check: { type: board, text: "Make 5 values (from 0 to 12) with a mean of 6 and a median of 5.", when: "n = 5 and m = 6 and d = 5", explain: "For example 2, 4, 5, 9, 10: the middle is 5 and the total is 30." } ``` Then make a different set with the same mean and median. ## Make: a power bill on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A week of electricity readings with one hot day makes mean and median differ; the paper task makes them compute both and say why." hint: ["The median is the 4th value of 7.", "The total is 126."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A family's electricity use over 7 days, in kWh, was 14, 15, 15, 16, 17, 18 and 31 (the 31 was a heatwave day with the air conditioner on). How many kWh higher is the mean than the median?" steps: - ["Median: the list is in order, so the 4th of 7 is 16 kWh", "sort first, then take the middle"] - ["Mean: $14 + 15 + 15 + 16 + 17 + 18 + 31 = 126$, and $126 \\div 7 = 18$ kWh", "add, then share equally"] - ["$18 - 16 = 2$ kWh", "the mean is higher"] - ["The median is the better 'typical day'", "one very high day pulls the mean up"] picks: - step: 4 q: "Why is the mean higher than the median?" options: - "The one very high day pulls the mean up, but the median is just the middle value" - "The mean is always higher than the median" - "The two use different days" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Not always: it depends on the data. Look at the 31.", "Both use all seven days."] answer: "2" feedback: - ["18", "That is the mean. Take the median away from it."] - ["16", "That is the median. How much higher is the mean?"] criteria: - "I put the list in order before finding the median." - "I added and shared equally for the mean." - "I said what the 31 does to the mean and the median." explain: "Median 16 and mean 126 ÷ 7 = 18, so the mean is 2 kWh higher. The heatwave day pulls the mean up, and the median stays near a normal day." ``` Do this one in your book. The readings are made up, but your family's bill hides the same thing: an average that one hot day can lift. Work out the median and the mean, type how much higher the mean is, then choose the reason. **Also used in** - **Bills.** The 'average daily use' on an electricity bill is a mean. It hides hot and cold days and how many people live in the house. - **House prices and wages.** Reports often give a median, so that a few very high values do not drag the typical figure up. - **Sport.** Goals per game, runs per over and points per match are all summarised the same way. ```teacher summary: Students calculate the mean, median, mode and range of small data sets (odd and even counts, two modes, no mode, negative values), watching each measure move on a dot plot as values are added (AC9M7ST01, node 2). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can calculate the mean, median, mode and range of a data set. - I can find the median of an even number of values. - I can handle data with two modes or no mode. struggle: "Finding the median from a list that is not in order. Ask: is the list in order yet?" before: > Do the Run and Make boards yourself first. Students need Counting and measuring and division with decimals. This is a hinge: the next lesson asks which measure is most useful, which is meaningless if the values are wrong. The common mistake is taking the middle of the unsorted list for the median; it is planted in Leo's working and again in Practise. The board marks the mean with a triangle, the median with a dashed line and the range with an arrow; students can add values by clicking the line or typing them. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands; students who chose 5 found the median or mode." - "Run: ask why one big score moves the mean but not the median much." - "Investigate: model the even-count median with the sorted list on the board." - "Modify: for the keep-the-median task, ask which other values would work (only 6)." - "Make: collect different answers and check them on the board." - "Paper: the power bill is worked in books; the page marks the difference of mean and median (2) and the reason. Books out, and look for the list put in order before the median." stuck: - see: A student takes the middle of the unsorted list (Leo's mistake). ask: Is the list in order? fix: Sort first, then count to the middle. - see: A student gives the total as the mean. ask: How many values share that total? fix: Divide the total by the count. - see: A student picks one of two middle values for an even count. ask: Which value is exactly halfway between them? fix: Add the two middle values and halve. stretch: Find five whole numbers with mean 10, median 8 and mode 7. support: Write the data sorted on a strip of paper; fold to find the middle. leads: > Next: Which measure? (node 3), choosing the most useful measure for a data set. Where it leads: comparing data sets (this unit) and samples (Year 8). exit: q: Find the mean, median, mode and range of 6, 2, 9, 6, 7, 12. a: Mean 42 ÷ 6 = 7; median (6 + 7) ÷ 2 = 6.5; mode 6; range 10. explain: > Four numbers sum up a data set: - **mean**: add the values, then divide by how many there are (3, 5, 5, 6, 11: 30 ÷ 5 = 6); - **median**: sort the values and take the middle one; for an even count, halfway between the two middle values; - **mode**: the most common value (there can be two, or none); - **range**: highest minus lowest (11 − 3 = 8), a measure of spread. ```
